 Order

Dated this the 08th day of October, 2025 Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.1990 of 2018 registered at the Erattupetta Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 406, 417 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 10 and 24 of the Emigration Act, 1983.

The crime was registered based on the 2nd respondent's complaint that he had paid Rs.5 lakhs to the petitioner's establishment named M/s. Ingenia Consultants Pvt Ltd, on the promise of securing a foreign student-cum-work visa.
The petitioner failed to arrange the visa as promised and refused to return the amount collected.
2. The police after investigation submitted Annexure2 Final Report and the case is now pending as C.C.No.50 of 2019 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Erattupetta.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Erattupetta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the petitioner contended that the allegations are patently false and only Rs.3,50,000/- was paid by the 2nd respondent.
That payment was made towards consultancy charges based on Annexure 3 agreement entered between the parties.
It was the 2nd respondent who had withdrawn from the agreement.

It is the contention of the learned Counsel that some amount was paid to the 2 nd respondent when he withdrew from the agreement and towards discharge of the balance liability, the petitioner issued a cheque for Rs.1,01,000/-, which, on presentation, was dishonoured for want of funds.
Thereupon, the 2nd respondent instituted a civil suit (O.S.No.47 of 2019) before the Munsiff Court, Erattupetta with the prayer for recovery of Rs.1,07,000/- with future interest.
4. It is contended that a dispute which is purely civil in nature is given the colour of a criminal offence 2025:KER:75574 by alleging breach of trust and cheating.
The incorporation of the offence under the Emigration Act is also illegal, since consultancy services being offered by the petitioner does not require license under the Emigration Authority.

sentences.text: 5. The 2nd respondent, though served with notice, has not appeared.
6. Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the number of crimes relating to visa fraud has increased exponentially and interference at a premature stage will embolden the perpetrators.
It is pointed out that CW2 has also given statement that he was duped by the petitioner's agency.

7. In spite of the appealing arguments advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioner, I refrain from invoking the inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, since consideration of the arguments call for 2025:KER:75574 appreciation of evidence, including documents which are not part of the Final Report.
Merely because a civil suit for recovery of money is filed, there is no bar in continuing with the criminal prosecution.
Moreover, the petitioner can move the trial court for discharge if that stage is not over or adduce evidence and raise the contentions at the appropriate stage.
The Criminal Miscellaneous Case is accordingly closed, without prejudice to the petitioner's right to move for discharge or to let in evidence, as the case may be.
